subject: surgery
title: Testicular Torsion and the Acute Scrotum

steps.tx: Twisting of the testis on its cord cutting off blood flow is **testicular torsion**. It strikes mostly adolescents and causes sudden severe scrotal pain with nausea. The testis lies high and horizontal, and every hour of delay lowers salvage. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Testicular torsion twists the cord, cuts blood flow, and every hour of delay lowers salvage.

vis.alt: Acute scrotum comparison of torsion and epididymitis.
vis.caption: Acute scrotum: torsion compared with epididymitis. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Relief of pain when the testis is lifted is called the **Prehn sign**. It traditionally suggests epididymitis rather than torsion, where lifting worsens pain. The sign is unreliable, so it must never delay exploration when torsion is possible. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: The Prehn sign suggests epididymitis when lifting relieves pain, but it must never delay exploration.

steps.tx: An abnormally mobile testis that can twist freely has a **bell clapper deformity**. The covering membrane attaches high on the cord, letting the testis swing like a bell clapper. Both sides often share the abnormality, so both are fixed at surgery. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: A bell clapper deformity lets the testis swing freely, and both sides are fixed at surgery.

steps.tx: Infection of the epididymis and testis causing gradual scrotal pain is **epididymo-orchitis**. It usually follows urinary or sexually transmitted infection and brings fever with urinary symptoms. Antibiotics and support treat it, though torsion must first be excluded. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Epididymo-orchitis causes gradual pain with fever and needs antibiotics once torsion is excluded.

steps.tx: Surgical untwisting and fixation of the testis is called **orchidopexy**. The surgeon inspects colour after untwisting and removes the testis only if dead. The opposite testis is fixed at the same operation to prevent future torsion. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Orchidopexy untwists and fixes the testis, and the opposite side is fixed at the same operation.

steps.tx: The golden window for saving a twisted testis is roughly **six hours**. Beyond a day, most testes are lost even after untwisting. This is why suspected torsion goes straight to theatre without waiting for scans in clear cases. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Saving a twisted testis is likeliest within six hours, so clear cases go straight to theatre.

steps.tx: Absence of the reflex that lifts the testis when the inner thigh is stroked is the **cremasteric reflex** loss. It is commonly absent in torsion and present in epididymitis. Like all single signs, it supports but never replaces clinical judgement. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Loss of the cremasteric reflex supports torsion, though no single sign replaces clinical judgement.

vis.alt: Scrotal palpation technique and comparison of findings.
vis.caption: Scrotal palpation and reflex assessment. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Doppler ultrasound may help only when the diagnosis is genuinely uncertain, a limited **imaging role**. Blood flow absence supports torsion, but normal flow does not exclude it. Imaging must never postpone theatre in a classic presentation. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Doppler helps only in genuinely uncertain cases and must never postpone theatre in classic torsion.

steps.tx: Manual untwisting by hand is a temporary measure called **manual detorsion**. It can relieve pain while theatre is prepared but does not replace surgery. Fixation is still required because retwisting is common. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Manual detorsion can relieve pain temporarily, but surgical fixation is still required afterwards.
